newsitem.title: UK: Gallaher move prompts new look at tobacco sector.
newsitem.headline: Gallaher move prompts new look at tobacco sector.

text.p: The prospect of Britain's biggest cigarette maker, Gallaher, joining the country's FTSE 100 index next year has prompted a new look at investment opportunities in the British tobacco industry, analysts said on Wednesday.

Yet with the domestic cigarette market largely stagnant, the driving force behind the sector in the near-term is likely to be continued bid speculation, analysts said. And some say Gallaher may have a short life as an independent group.
American Brands plans to spin off the British-based Gallaher, maker of top selling brands Silk Cut and Benson & Hedges.
"There probably will be even more bid speculation surrounding Gallaher because it has the premium brands," said one analyst.
Gallaher and Imperial Tobacco have dominant market shares in Britain about 39 and 38 percent respectively. Their lack of sales in the United States shields them from U.S. litigation risks.
Talk of a takeover bid for Imperial, one of the companies demerged from conglomerate Hanson Plc, helped lift the price of Imperial shares immediately after its flotation earlier this month.

B.A.T Industries, which owns Brown & Williamson, maker of Kent, Kool and State Express in the United States, was tipped as a possible buyer of Imperial, and some say it may have its sights on Gallaher.

Imperial and Gallaher are seen as attractive targets because they have no exposure to U.S. litigation. There has been a growing threat of litigation in the UK, but the suits are years away from getting into the courts.
"The key question is not what happens in the courts in the UK, it's what happens in the U.S.," said SBC Warburg analyst Mark Duffy. "The only thing for certain is that there will be a lot of action."
Duffy has a "hold" rating on B.A.T shares, which have tumbled in recent months because of its U.S. exposure.
"The stock is likely to be very volatile for the next few months as U.S. court cases come up," Duffy said. "The critical phase will have been completed by mid-'97 and we'll have a clearer view."
But Duffy maintains an "overweight" rating on Imperial and said an industry predator like B.A.T, which lacks sales in the UK, could launch a bid for Gallaher.
